newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - PLDT prices entice.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - PLDT prices entice.

text.p: News Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co's global bond priced overnight was the highlight of an otherwise slow Asian debt market Wednesday.
PLDT's US$200 million 7.85 percent bond due March 2007 was priced to yield 150 basis points over comparable U.S. Treasuries.
Its US$300 million 8.35 percent bond due March 2017 was priced to yield 170 basis points over Treasuries.
Goldman Sachs and Citicorp were the lead managers.
The issue was more than double its originally intended US$200 million.
Goldman Sachs said about two-thirds of the 20-year tranche was taken up by U.S. investors, as was about half of the 10-year tranche.
U.S. investors typically prefer longer-dated issues.
"But there also was a lot of interest in the the 20-year from Asian accounts," a Goldman Sachs syndicate source said.
She said the issue attracted some investors that usually only invest in investment grade paper.
"PLDT is the type of credit that attracts cross-over investment grade buyers in addition to the usual high yield buyers and emerging markets funds," she said.
The PLDT bond was rated BB-plus by Standard and Poor's Corp and Ba2 by Moody's Investors Service.
S&P raised the long-term foreign currency rating of PLDT to BB-plus from BB on February 21 following its upgrade of the Republic of the Phillipines sovereign debt to BB-plus from BB.
"When S&P upgraded the Philippines it said the outlook is still positive, so people went out and bought the PLDT bond," said a trader at a U.S. bank in Hong Kong.
The market has been very positive on the Philippines and pricing for Philippine issues has come in tremendously over the last year.
For example, PLDT's global bond launched in June 1996 paid 175 basis points over Treasuries for the 10-year tranche and 240 basis points for the 10-year tranche.
In other news, Thailand's PTT Exploration and Production, the exploration arm of the Petroleum Authoritiy of Thailand, said it plans to issue bonds in foreign markets worth US$200 million this year.
A unit of South Korea's Kohap launched a US$60 million floating rate note, arranger KDB Asia said.

On Thursday, Sri Lanka will roadshow its US$50 million FRN in Hong Kong. The FRN, which is Sri Lanka's first international capital markets issue in many years, is lead managed by Citicorp. -- Andrea Ricci (852) 2843-6371 fax (852) 2845-0636
